label: token after a u/s/v-initial prefix of p/l/b/h-type letters (steps 3-5)
explanation: Very sparse (about 1 in 10k sequences), weak feature (max 0.17). It fires almost only in the original phase at steps 3-5. The sequence starts with u (72% of mass; s or v for most of the rest), and every token so far comes from a small set {u,s,v,p,l,b,h,k,x,r}, typically u p l / u l b / u s p b. The previous token is l, b or h. The current token is a letter outside that set, most often y (42% of mass), then n, w, j, r. The strongest examples are u s p b [y] and u p l h [y]. It never fires in the copy phase, at steps 0-2, or at step 6 or later, and it fires only once on <DEL>. The predicate gets 85% of activation mass but only about 5% precision. Most matching prefixes (e.g. u r b s, s b h 0) do not fire, so it looks like a narrow region of hidden-state space reached by this prefix family, not a clean token rule. Magnitude is highest with first token u and current token y; other variations were not checked further.
